The drama was absolutely amazing, and almost every episode was enjoyable until Shamir and Shibra got married. After their marriage, the story somehow felt different, and the quality of the episodes was not as strong as before.

However, all of the actors did a fantastic job portraying their characters. The character of Fazal Baksh was especially entertaining. He was incredibly funny, and his dialogues were outstanding. Many of his scenes made the drama even more enjoyable.

The earlier episodes were truly mind-blowing and kept me hooked from the beginning. The story, suspense, and character development were excellent. Unfortunately, I don’t think the ending lived up to the standard set by the earlier episodes. While the drama as a whole was still very good, the finale could have been written and executed much better.

Overall, it was a wonderful drama with memorable characters, great performances, and many unforgettable moments, but the ending was not as satisfying as I had hoped.

I didn’t like the way Shamir’s relationship with his father-in-law was handled in the last moments of the story. From the beginning of the drama, Mr. Suleman and Shamir shared a very strong bond. In fact, Shamir didn’t even seem to have such a close relationship with his own father. Mr. Suleman cared for him like his own son, hugged him, gave him a place in his home, and treated him as part of the family.

I understand that Shamir wanted to protect his political party, but he could have at least visited Mr. Suleman in jail, even secretly. At the very least, he should not have spoken those words in front of the media. Shamir knew that his father-in-law was innocent, yet he did not have the courage to tell the truth publicly. How can he be a leader of justice if he cannot stand up for an innocent man?

I think if Shamir’s mother had still been alive, she would have had the courage to openly declare that Mr. Suleman was innocent. She never cared about public opinion when it came to doing the right thing, and that was why people respected her as a leader of justice.

I know politics is not easy, but throughout the drama politicians were shown to have the power to get people released from jail with a single phone call. Yet Shamir could do absolutely nothing for the man who treated him like a son. In the end, Mr. Suleman died, and Shamir did not even investigate what had really happened. How could a man simply die or suicide  in jail without anyone looking into it?

Another thing I disliked was that Shamir barely showed any emotion after Mr. Suleman’s death. One of the reasons Shamir loved Shibra was because of her honesty and kindness. He valued her character more than her beauty. In the same way, he should have admired and respected his father-in-law even more. After Mr. Suleman’s death, Shamir should have been deeply emotional and regretful, realizing that his own mistakes had cost him such a noble man.

He failed to protect him. At the very least, he should have felt guilty for putting Mr. Suleman in such a vulnerable position. Giving an honest officer a major role in fighting corruption could naturally make him a target of false accusations. Why didn’t Shamir take precautions earlier? Why didn’t he visit him in jail with Shibra during the final episodes?

There were also some inconsistencies in the last episodes. Mehrin threatened Shibra, yet Shibra never told Shamir about it. Even after being attacked, she never seriously suspected Mehrin or mentioned her name. Similarly, Mr. Suleman was told that Shibra’s life could be in danger, yet he never informed Shamir about it. These plot points made the final episodes feel disconnected from the rest of the drama.

Ishq Murshid — Review 🇧🇩

Just finished Ishq Murshid, and honestly, I really enjoyed the journey. Shahmeer and Shibra were the heart of the drama. Bilal Abbas Khan did an amazing job portraying both Shahmeer and Fazal Bakhsh—the contrast between his serious, intelligent personality and Fazal Bakhsh’s innocent, funny side was one of the best things about the drama. Durefishan Saleem was equally impressive as Shibra, and their chemistry felt natural and enjoyable throughout.

I also liked the supporting characters, especially Zubaida and Safdar Shah, because they added more depth to the family and political side of the story. The drama had a good mix of romance, comedy, emotions and mystery, and the characters kept me interested for most of the journey.

My biggest disappointment was the ending. Everything suddenly moved way too fast, and it honestly felt like several important parts of the story were skipped or rushed. Some characters and conflicts deserved a proper conclusion instead of being wrapped up so quickly.

Overall, Ishq Murshid was a beautiful and entertaining watch with great performances and memorable characters. I just wish the writers had given the ending more time and depth.

8/10 ❤️🇧🇩

The drama shows the hero following the ideals of his mother, who was an honest leader trying to run the country with integrity. On the other hand, the heroine also shares similar values. Everything builds toward a strong message of honest leadership and commitment.

However, in the end, the hero fails to handle the party and decides to step away from leadership. This feels inconsistent. Throughout the drama, he is inspired by his mother’s ideals, and even in his imagination, she encourages him to carry forward her vision. But ultimately, he gives up, which contradicts that entire buildup.

Because of this, the ending doesn’t feel satisfying or meaningful. It raises the question—what was the actual message of the drama?
